text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- In a challenge to South Korean President Kim Young Sam, opposition parties reject his offer to re-open debate on new labour law as nation's top strike leader heads protest march through Seoul.
- Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong and Education Minister Lee Yock Suan suing defeated Workers' Party candidate Tang Liang Hong for allegedly defaming them in a police report on January 1.
- Man dies after Mercedes-Benz bursts into flames in expressway accident.
- New three-day test for national service enlistees in a military environment will be introduced during basic military training to pick those with officer potential.
- Applications to resell Housing Board flats dip below 10,000 mark in final quarter of 1996, surrendering gains in previous two quarters.
- Economic Development Board bullish on outlook for Singapore communications and media industries for next two years despite increasing regional competition.
- Door maker Chuan Soon Huat Industrial Group turns in best first-day performance among new mainboard listings since beginning of last year.
- Huge wave of stagging lifts price of debutante Chuan Soon Huat Holdings to dazzling intra-day high of 63.5 cents, 81.4 percent above offer price of 35 cents.
- HDB resale flat volume reaches 39,079 in 1996 despite slightly weak last quarter, surpassing 1995's record volume of 33,462 by 17 percent.
- Steep early slide on Wall Street drags European equities from record levels.
- Singapore Airlines may have no choice but to buy super jumbos from European consortium Airbus if Boeing does not reconsider decision to drop out of race to develop the aircraft.
- Aztech Systems will raise about Singapore $21 million through private placement to repay bank borrowings.
- Joseph Gondobintoro, Singapore-based Indonesian white knight of video tape manufacturer Electro Magnetics, sued by Hong Kong arm of now defunct Bank of Credit and Commerce International.
- Uraco Holdings managing director Lim Ee Ann to leave position next month, with his place taken by three divisional managing directors.
